topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets the pedagogical context for studying cancer biology.

topics.label: Carcinogenesis as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations disrupt normal developmental differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and the progression from benign to malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the histological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant tumors through mechanisms of local tissue invasion and metastatic spread.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the naming rules and notable exceptions used to categorize benign and malignant tumors by their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how primary tumor expansion and distant metastases physically and metabolically disrupt organ function to cause severe illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the frequency of benign and malignant tumor types across human populations and throughout diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical cancer detection and screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: They assess the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, and relative effectiveness of population screening programs across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture summary and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and directing students to upcoming practical sessions.
